prompt:
Add a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown` (and `markdown.markdown`): a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0, that shifts the level of every heading Markdown produces by that many (an `h1` becomes an `h2` with 1), never beyond `h6`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- It applies to hash and underline headings, and to headings from extensions such as `md_in_html`.
- The `toc` extension sees the shifted levels (its tokens and `toc_depth`).
- The command line gets `--heading-offset N`.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: I added the `heading_offset` option (a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0) to `markdown.Markdown` and `markdown.markdown`, plus `--heading-offset N` on the command line. The full test suite passes (1145 tests, 112 skipped). Any other value raises `ValueError`, including floats, strings, `None` and booleans. An out-of-range or non-integer value on the command line exits with a usage error instead. A new tree step shifts every heading in the document, capped at `h6`, just before `toc` runs. So it covers hash and underline headings, `md_in_html` and footnote content, and `toc` sees the shifted levels in its tokens and `toc_depth`. If `toc`'s `baselevel` is also set, it adds on top of the offset. Headings written as raw HTML that Markdown doesn't parse are left unchanged. The offset is checked only when the object is created, so setting `md.heading_offset` later is not validated. I added tests, docs (library, command line, `toc`) and a changelog entry under `[Unreleased]`, which has no issue number. flake8 isn't installed, so linting wasn't run; I only checked line lengths.
